Road-ready vehicles, faster billing, cleaner trip settlements.

For full-truckload and part-truckload transporters, fleet owners, contract fleets and operators who also run attached market vehicles. We automate document and maintenance tracking, e-way bill validity, delay alerts, POD-to-invoice and trip settlements around your TMS, GPS and accounts, with your fleet manager and finance team approving every decision.

What makes fleet & road transport different

  • Licenses, permits, fitness certificates, PUC and insurance expire on different dates across owned and attached vehicles.

  • Physical PODs arrive weeks after delivery, so billing waits and detention charges go unclaimed.

  • Trip advances and expense claims are settled by hand with little link to fuel card, FASTag or GPS data.

  • E-way bills expire while trucks wait at hubs or consignee gates, and the team finds out at a checkpoint.

  • Shippers hear about breakdowns and delays when they call, not from the transporter.

Where automation helps fleet & road transport

  • Driver and vehicle document register

    Documents are collected, checked against VAHAN and SARATHI records and tracked to expiry, and assignment is blocked when something lapses.

  • Preventive maintenance from odometer data

    GPS odometer readings drive service, tire and inspection reminders, and drivers report defects with photos and voice notes on WhatsApp.

  • E-way bill validity watch

    Validity is compared with the GPS-based ETA, with alerts in the extension window and Part B reminders when goods change vehicles.

  • Digital POD to invoice

    PODs captured in the driver app or on WhatsApp become draft invoices, with detention charges calculated from recorded arrival and unloading times.

  • Trip expense and fuel settlement

    Receipts are read from photos and checked against fuel card, FASTag and GPS data before the fleet manager approves the settlement.

  • Delay alerts to shippers

    Breakdowns, no-movement and ETA slippage create an exception with an owner and a shipper update before the promised delivery time passes.

Vehicle & driver assignmentStandard4–6 weeks

Driver and rider onboarding with document expiry alerts

Collect and verify driver and rider documents at onboarding, track every expiry date for licenses, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness and permits, and stop a vehicle or driver with a lapsed document from being assigned.

Fleet & road transport · Courier & last-mile delivery

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Licenses, registration certificates, insurance, PUC certificates, fitness certificates and permits expire on different dates and sit in folders, WhatsApp photos and spreadsheets. Lapses come to light at a checkpoint, during an accident claim or in a client audit. Courier networks onboarding many riders, including riders on their own two-wheelers, face the same problem at higher volume.

Trigger

A new driver or rider applies, a vehicle is added to the fleet, a document enters its reminder window before expiry, or a trip assignment is about to be confirmed.

How it runs

  1. Collect documents through a WhatsApp Flow or onboarding form after a clear notice and consent, accepting DigiLocker-issued copies the applicant chooses to share.
  2. Use OCR and an AI model to read names, numbers and expiry dates, and check license and registration details against VAHAN and SARATHI records through ULIP or an authorized verification provider.
  3. Store each document with its expiry date in a compliance register per driver and vehicle, and flag mismatches such as a license class that does not cover the vehicle type.
  4. Remind the driver, the vehicle owner and the fleet manager at agreed intervals before each expiry, and collect the renewed document in the same chat.
  5. Check validity at trip assignment and hold confirmation of any driver or vehicle with a lapsed document until the fleet manager clears it.
  6. Report upcoming expiries, lapses and renewals by branch, vendor and vehicle type.

Human checkpoint

The fleet or HR manager approves every onboarding after reviewing flagged mismatches, and decides any exception to the assignment hold. Background verification results are reviewed by a person; the AI model only reads and compares documents.

Systems it connects

  • DigiLocker

Data & consent

Driver and rider documents are personal data. We collect only what the role and the law require, with a clear notice and consent, keep documents encrypted with access limited to HR and fleet managers, and do not store full Aadhaar numbers. Documents of drivers and riders who leave are deleted after the agreed retention period.

What we deliver

  • Onboarding Flow and document checklist by role
  • Compliance register for drivers, riders and vehicles
  • Expiry reminder schedule and templates
  • Validity check at trip assignment
  • Expiry and lapse dashboard

How we measure it

  • Vehicles or drivers with a lapsed document
  • Onboarding time from application to approval
  • Renewals completed before expiry
  • Assignments held for lapsed documents

Vehicle & driver assignmentStandard3–5 weeks

Preventive maintenance and tire reminders from odometer data

Use GPS odometer readings and service history to schedule preventive maintenance, tire rotation and inspections for each vehicle, warn dispatch before a due vehicle is assigned, and track work orders to closure.

Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Service intervals are tracked in a register or in the mechanic's memory. Vehicles skip services during peak season, breakdowns strand loads mid-route, and tires and batteries are replaced without history. Dispatch cannot see which vehicles need workshop time when planning the week.

Trigger

A vehicle's GPS odometer reading crosses a service threshold, a date-based interval is reached, a driver reports a defect, or a vehicle is selected for a trip.

How it runs

  1. Pull daily odometer and engine-hour readings from the GPS or telematics platform and reconcile them with trip and fuel records.
  2. Calculate the next service, tire rotation, battery check and inspection due points for each vehicle from the maintenance plan and service history.
  3. Alert the maintenance supervisor and dispatcher as a vehicle approaches a due point, and suggest a workshop slot that fits the trip plan.
  4. Let drivers report defects with photos and voice notes on WhatsApp; an AI model turns them into structured defect reports for the supervisor.
  5. Create and track work orders with parts, cost and downtime, and mark the vehicle unavailable in the TMS until the supervisor closes the job.
  6. Report planned and unplanned maintenance, downtime and cost per kilometer by vehicle and route.

Human checkpoint

The maintenance supervisor decides whether a defect makes a vehicle unfit to run, approves any deferral of a due service and signs off completed work orders. Brake, steering, tire and other safety-related defects reported by drivers always go to a person.

In transit, at hubs & at customsStandard3–5 weeks

E-way bill validity watch with extension and Part B alerts

Compare each active e-way bill's validity with the vehicle's GPS position and ETA, warn the trip owner before expiry, prompt Part B updates when goods change vehicles, and prepare extension details for an authorized user to submit.

Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Trucks wait at hubs, break down or queue at consignee gates while e-way bills run out, and transshipments need Part B updated before goods move to another vehicle. Operations teams often find out when an officer stops the vehicle, and goods moving on an expired e-way bill can be detained with penalties.

Trigger

An e-way bill is linked to a trip, the GPS-based ETA moves past the validity end, the bill enters its extension window, or a vehicle change is recorded at a hub.

How it runs

  1. Read the active e-way bills for each trip through the client's GSP or ERP integration, with validity end, distance and vehicle number.
  2. Compare remaining validity with the GPS-based ETA and current position, and flag bills that will expire before delivery.
  3. Alert the trip owner when the extension window opens, with the current location, remaining distance and a draft reason, such as transshipment or accident, for the authorized user to confirm.
  4. When a vehicle change is logged at a hub, remind the hub team to update Part B with the new vehicle number before loading.
  5. Prepare the extension details for an authorized user to review and submit through the portal or API, then record the new validity on the trip.
  6. Report bills expired in transit, extensions and late Part B updates by lane, branch and customer.

Human checkpoint

An authorized user at the transporter reviews and submits every extension and Part B update. The automation never generates, extends or cancels an e-way bill on its own, and any interception or detention by officers is handled by the branch manager.

In transit, at hubs & at customsAdvanced6–8 weeks

Proactive delay and SLA breach alerts with customer updates

Watch every shipment and warehouse order against its promised date or SLA, flag delays, stuck consignments, missed cut-offs and free-time risks early, give each exception an owner, and tell the customer before they have to ask.

Courier & last-mile delivery · Freight forwarding & customs · Warehousing & 3PL · Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Tracking data exists in the TMS, carrier portals, GPS dashboards and the WMS, but nobody watches all of it against what was promised. Delays surface when the customer calls, key accounts hear about rollovers or breakdowns late, warehouse orders miss the carrier cut-off unnoticed, and the same lanes, hubs and carriers fail repeatedly without data to show it.

Trigger

A milestone is missed or late against plan, the ETA moves past the promised date, a shipment shows no scan or GPS movement beyond the agreed limit, or an SLA timer nears breach.

How it runs

  1. Pull milestones from the TMS, courier and carrier tracking APIs, GPS platforms, WMS order status and shipping line or airline feeds into one timeline with the promised date and SLA.
  2. Run rules for missed pickups, no-movement, stuck-at-hub, ETA slippage, vessel rollovers, free-time expiry and warehouse orders not packed before the carrier cut-off, tuned per lane, service and client.
  3. Create an exception with an owner, reason code and deadline in the control-tower queue, and alert the owner in Slack.
  4. Send the consignee or shipper an approved WhatsApp, SMS or email update with the revised ETA; for key accounts, the account manager approves the message first.
  5. Escalate exceptions still open near the SLA limit to the branch or operations head.
  6. Report exceptions, causes and SLA performance by lane, hub, carrier and client for the weekly review.

Human checkpoint

Control-tower executives own every exception, confirm the reason before messages go to key accounts, and decide rerouting, upgrades and any cost or claim commitment. Customers are never promised compensation by an automated message.

  • Carrier, shipping line and airline tracking APIs
  • GPS or telematics platform

  • Exception resolution time
  • Where-is-my-shipment contacts per thousand shipments

Delivery, NDR & proof of deliveryStandard4–6 weeks

Digital POD capture and freight invoice drafting

Capture proof of delivery with photos, stamp or OTP, unloading times and remarks in the driver app or on WhatsApp, match it to the LR, and turn complete PODs into draft freight invoices with detention and other charges for finance to approve.

Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Physical POD copies travel back with drivers or by courier, sometimes weeks after delivery. Billing waits for them, shippers reject invoices without a POD, detention and unloading charges go unclaimed because nobody recorded the times, and receivables stretch while finance chases paperwork.

Trigger

A driver marks a trip delivered in the app, sends a POD photo on WhatsApp, or the consignee confirms receipt with an OTP or e-signature.

How it runs

  1. Collect POD photos, consignee stamp or signature, OTP confirmation, arrival and unloading times and any shortage or damage remarks through the driver app or WhatsApp.
  2. Use OCR and an AI model to read the LR number, consignee stamp, date and remarks, match them to the trip, and flag missing stamps, unreadable images or noted shortages.
  3. Calculate freight from the contract rate card and add detention, loading, multi-point or toll charges from recorded times and the contract terms.
  4. Create a draft invoice in the accounting system with POD and LR images attached, and route it to the billing executive for review.
  5. Send approved invoices with PODs to the shipper's billing contact or portal, and track acknowledgement and payment due dates.
  6. Report POD collection time, unbilled trips and invoice disputes by customer and branch.

Human checkpoint

The billing executive reviews every draft invoice, and the finance controller approves detention or other charges outside the contract and any credit note. PODs with shortage or damage remarks go to the claims owner before billing.

  • Invoice disputes for missing PODs
  • Detention charges billed against detention recorded

Billing, settlement & reviewStandard4–6 weeks

Trip expense and fuel claims with GPS and fuel card checks

Let drivers submit fuel, toll, loading and repair expenses with receipt photos on WhatsApp, check them against fuel card, FASTag and GPS data, and give the fleet manager a short list of exceptions to approve before the trip is settled.

Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Drivers carry cash advances and return with a bundle of receipts. Accounts check them by hand against trip sheets, fuel bills do not tie to kilometers driven, toll claims overlap with FASTag deductions, and settlements drag on. Honest drivers wait for their money while questionable claims slip through.

Trigger

A driver sends an expense photo or voice note during a trip, a trip is closed in the TMS, or fuel card and FASTag statements arrive.

How it runs

  1. Collect receipts, odometer photos and voice notes from drivers on WhatsApp during the trip and attach them to the trip record.
  2. Use OCR and an AI model to extract date, amount, vendor, fuel quantity and location from each receipt, and ask the driver for anything missing.
  3. Cross-check fuel against fuel card transactions and expected consumption for the vehicle and route, tolls against FASTag statements, and claimed locations against the GPS track.
  4. Calculate the settlement against the advance and the expense policy, and list exceptions such as duplicate tolls, fuel beyond tolerance or missing receipts.
  5. Send the fleet manager the settlement with exceptions for approval, then post the approved entry to accounts and inform the driver.

Human checkpoint

The fleet manager approves every settlement and decides on exceptions after hearing the driver. Flags are prompts for a conversation, not findings of misconduct, and any deduction or disciplinary step is decided by the manager and HR.
